subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Future of Car Design
description: A 60-second lesson on The Future of Car Design.

hook.text: Without engines, radiators, or exhaust pipes, electric cars free designers from a century of constraints.

buildup.text: Flat battery floors create cabin space that resembles a living room more than a traditional car interior.

discovery.text: Some concept EVs have no steering wheel—in a fully autonomous future, the cabin becomes a mobile office or lounge.

twist.text: With fewer mechanical parts, 3D printing and AI-generated designs could make each car uniquely personalized.

climax.text: The car of 2040 may look nothing like today's—more pod than vehicle, shaped by software rather than aerodynamics.

punchline.text: When the engine disappears, the entire car gets reinvented.

quiz.question: How does removing the engine affect car design?
options: Designers are freed from traditional mechanical constraints

details.summary: Electric drivetrains, autonomous systems, and new materials are freeing car designers from a century of combustion-era constraints, enabling radical new shapes and interior layouts.
details.whyItMatters: Without a bulky engine up front, designers can rethink proportions, add larger cabins, and create interiors focused on comfort and productivity rather than just driving.
takeaways: Flat battery packs enable a skateboard platform design
No engine means more flexible front-end styling
Autonomous cars may feature swiveling seats and work desks

faq.question: Why do so many new EVs look similar?
faq.answer: Aerodynamic efficiency is critical for maximizing range, pushing designers toward smooth, teardrop-like shapes. As battery technology improves, designers will have more freedom to differentiate.

faq.question: Will steering wheels disappear in future cars?
faq.answer: At full Level 5 autonomy, steering wheels and pedals become unnecessary. Regulators may still require them as a backup for many years until the technology is proven beyond doubt.
